rationale: Both candidates are essentially the same AAA PRS (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same method PRS-CS, same variant count, same EUR-only evaluation ancestry, same publication/date), so endpoint fidelity and structural signals do not differentiate. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the only performance evidence is full-model discrimination; in that limited context PGS003973 shows a higher reported C-index (0.882 with CI) with only basic demographic covariates (age, age^2, sex), whereas PGS003972 reports a lower AUROC (0.69) with covariates unknown. Because full-model metrics are not PRS-comparable and covariates differ/are unclear, confidence is low, but the cleaner disclosed covariates plus stronger reported discrimination favors PGS003973.

PGS004913 is a disease-focused score explicitly developed for alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis in heavy drinkers, with tightly aligned trait_reported/phenotyping_reported to the target alcoholic liver cirrhosis and clean basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). It also provides a meaningful PRS effect size signal (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4), whereas PGS000704 comes from a broad UKB biomarker genetics framework context and only reports a full-model C-index (0.711) plus a modest HR (1.18) without any PRS-only AUC/R2; the full-model metric is not PRS-comparable. Both are EUR-focused, but PGS000704’s larger training/validation size does not outweigh the stronger endpoint fidelity and more directly PRS-informative effect-size evidence in PGS004913.

PGS001262 has slightly better PRS-comparable performance on the selected European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683 vs 0.58233; PGS-only R2 0.01304 vs 0.01228) while both models share the same study family (UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet), identical basic covariates, and similar ancestry evaluation setup. Endpoint fidelity favors PGS001262 as a direct doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype, whereas PGS001261 is explicitly time-to-event (TTE), which is a mild mismatch for a generic angina pectoris target. Training/validation size and variant count (higher for PGS001261) are weaker tie-breakers here and do not outweigh the cleaner endpoint plus marginally stronger PRS-only metrics for PGS001262.

Both candidates map cleanly to angina pectoris (EFO match; PheCode 411.3 in PGS005052 vs doctor-diagnosed angina in PGS001262). However, PGS001262 provides PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683 and PGS-only R²=0.01304), enabling a clean comparison and a heritability sanity check (R² stays below the local h2_obs ceiling). In contrast, PGS005052 lacks PGS-only AUC/R² and reports only a full-model C-index (0.766) plus an OR=1.491, making its discrimination evidence less directly comparable as a standalone PRS. While PGS005052 has a more genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) and far more variants, the missing PRS-only metrics reduce support relative to PGS001262’s explicit PRS-only evaluation.

PGS001261 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.5823) and PGS-only R² (0.0123) with basic covariates, allowing a clean PRS signal check (and the R² is plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling). PGS005052 lacks PRS-only AUC/R² entirely and only shows a full-model C-index plus an OR, so its discrimination is not directly comparable for PRS ranking. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (angina pectoris), but PGS001261’s time-to-event framing is a mild endpoint penalty; still, the absence of PRS-only metrics in PGS005052 outweighs its larger variant count and multi-ancestry context here.

Both candidates match the target trait well (same trait_reported/trait_efo). However, PGS000753 is a very sparse P+T score (29 variants) with no PRS-comparable performance metrics reported (only an OR=1.37 per SD, moderate) and a prevalent-case phenotype. PGS003973 is a disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis-derived genome-wide PRS-CS score (~1.1M variants), which is structurally better suited to capture polygenic signal; its reported C-index=0.882 is full-model (age/age^2/sex) and thus not PRS-only, but the covariates are basic and the endpoint is a direct AAA diagnosis. Given the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 for both, the stronger method/variant coverage and broader development context favor PGS003973.

Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS001777 is more disease-focused and endpoint-faithful in context: it comes from a cirrhosis-specific study (“genetic risk score and diabetes predict development of alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers”) and reports a strong discrimination signal via OR(top 20% vs bottom 20%)=6.18 plus a beta estimate, whereas PGS000704 is from a broad biomarker genetics framework paper and only shows a modest per-SD HR=1.18. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2 (both only show full-model AUROC/C-index), so the small full-model difference (0.711 vs 0.671) is not a reliable PRS comparator—especially since PGS000704’s metric is from a time-to-event model with explicit covariates. Despite PGS000704’s much larger training/validation and higher variant count, the combination of disease-specific study focus and stronger effect-size evidence makes PGS001777 better-supported for alcoholic liver cirrhosis.

PGS001267 has better endpoint fidelity to the target trait (ankylosing spondylitis) with a direct disease phenotype (“Ankylosing spondylitis” / phenotyping_reported: “Ankylosing spondylitis”), whereas PGS001268 is explicitly time-to-event (“Ankylosing spondylitis (time-to-event)” / phenotyping_reported: “TTE ankylosing spondylitis”), which is a mild mismatch for a generic disease-risk target. Although PGS001268 shows slightly higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.7346 vs 0.7265; PGS-only R2 0.1023 vs 0.0988) with otherwise identical study family, covariates, variant count, training/validation sizes, and ancestry context, the metric gap is small and does not outweigh the cleaner phenotype match of PGS001267.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect sizes and structural signals. PGS002738 is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with far broader variant coverage (326,000 vs 858 for PGS002739) and shows a slightly stronger discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96 [1.54–2.51] vs 1.76 [1.32–2.34]). PGS002739 is evaluated in African American samples (useful for AFR deployment) but is a sparse gene-based score with weaker OR evidence and no compensating PRS-only metrics. With endpoint fidelity essentially tied and covariates unknown for both, the stronger OR and much higher genome-wide coverage favor PGS002738.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis) and both use only basic demographic/PC-style covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). However, PGS001267 provides explicit PRS-comparable performance metrics in Europeans (PGS-only AUROC=0.7265; PGS-only R2=0.0988), whereas PGS002089 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) and has no PGS-only AUROC/R2, making its predictive evidence less directly comparable. Although PGS002089 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with many variants (22,026) and some multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of standard PRS-only discrimination metrics on the record makes it harder to judge support versus PGS001267’s clearly reported PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (AUROC=0.539, R2=0.00291) with basic covariates and these are interpretable/sane relative to the provided heritability ceiling guidance, whereas PGS004477 provides no AUROC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.20) and has unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability hard to judge. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (both map to EFO arthritis), but PGS001135’s phenotype is a generic arthritis (nos) match to the target, while PGS004477 is a narrower ICD10-style ‘Other arthritis’ label. Despite PGS004477’s genome-wide variant count and LDpred2 method, the lack of PRS-comparable validation metrics and unclear covariate context leaves it less well-supported than PGS001135.

PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: it has direct concept alignment (trait_reported and trait_efo both aortic stenosis) whereas PGS005255 is primarily a hemodynamic measurement score (trait_reported: mean pressure gradient; trait_efo includes aortic measurement), making it less endpoint-faithful despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported (incident aortic stenosis). Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, PRS-CS, EUR-only dev/eval, same covariates, same validation sample size, no PRS-only AUC/R2), so the differentiators are (1) endpoint fidelity and (2) slightly stronger effect size and training support: PGS005254 shows higher HR per SD (1.64 vs 1.53) and larger training n (205,483 vs 98,645).

PGS001268 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (plus CIs for AUROC), whereas PGS002089 provides no AUROC/R² and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919), which is less directly interpretable for PRS discrimination. Endpoint fidelity slightly favors PGS002089 (straight ankylosing spondylitis case status) over PGS001268’s time-to-event (TTE) phenotype, but both map to the same EFO and use only basic covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). Given the much clearer PRS-only metric evidence for PGS001268 and acceptable phenotype alignment, it wins despite the TTE penalty.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo are aortic stenosis; both are incident aortic stenosis in EUR-only DEV/EVAL) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on effect-size evidence and covariate comparability. PGS005254 reports a clear per-SD HR=1.64 with CI (1.50–1.78) under a relatively clean covariate set (age, age^2, sex, PCs), giving more interpretable PRS signal. PGS005252 reports a higher HR=1.92 and a C-index/full-model 0.87, but its covariates include multiple downstream clinical comorbidities/risk factors (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), making the reported discrimination less PRS-comparable and potentially more covariate-driven; its HR also lacks a CI here. Training/validation sizes differ but are weak tie-breakers. Overall, PGS005254 has cleaner, more directly PRS-informative evidence on the visible fields.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291), allowing a heritability-ceiling sanity check and showing the PRS contribution is small but quantified. It also uses only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and has multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004547 has no AUC/R² reported at all (only an OR=1.26, which is weak-to-moderate) and lists covariates as Unknown, reducing comparability and interpretability despite its larger variant count and EUR-only evaluation. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (arthritis umbrella), so the decisive difference is the presence of clean PGS-only metrics and broader evaluation in PGS001135.

PGS005252 is the better-supported choice for the target trait aortic stenosis because its endpoint alignment is exact (trait_reported/trait_efo both aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported incident aortic stenosis cases), whereas PGS005255 is primarily labeled as a valve-function quantitative trait (trait_reported: Mean pressure gradient; trait_efo includes aortic measurement), making it a less direct match despite mentioning incident aortic stenosis in phenotyping. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect-size and design signals: PGS005252 shows a stronger HR per SD (1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255), suggesting stronger PRS discrimination. PGS005252’s reported C-index=0.87 is full-model and covariate-inflated (many clinical covariates), but PGS005255 provides no comparable discrimination metric at all; thus the stronger effect size plus cleaner trait labeling favors PGS005252. Ancestry is identical (EUR-only dev/eval) and validation sizes are not decisive.

PGS002738 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_efo is exactly "alcohol dependence" and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported are "Alcohol use disorder" (a near-synonymous clinical diagnosis). It also shows a reasonably strong discriminative signal via an OR top 10% vs rest of 1.96 (1.54–2.51), which is meaningful evidence even without PRS-only AUC/R2. In contrast, PGS000201 is mapped to a weaker/less direct concept (trait_efo "alcohol dependence measurement" and trait_reported "Problematic alcohol use"), and its only PRS-comparable metric is a small incremental ΔR²=0.01192; while it has explicit basic covariates, that doesn’t compensate for the less faithful endpoint. Both are EUR-evaluated with similar validation N, so endpoint fidelity and effect-size support favor PGS002738.

Both candidates match the target trait well (AAA; same EFO). However, PGS003972 is built with a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) and ~1.1M variants from a large multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis context, which is structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than PGS000753’s very sparse P+T score with 29 variants. Performance reporting is imperfect for both (no PGS-only AUC/R2); PGS003972’s AUROC=0.69 is full-model and thus not directly comparable, but PGS000753 provides only an OR per SD (1.37, moderate) and no AUC/R2 either. Covariates are known and basic for PGS000753 (age/sex/PCs), while PGS003972 has unknown covariates (confidence penalty), yet the overall evidence package (method + genome-wide coverage + disease-focused meta-analysis cohorts) favors PGS003972 over the older sparse model.

PGS002739 is the better match to the target trait alcohol dependence on endpoint fidelity: it is explicitly an Alcohol use disorder case/control-style endpoint (trait_efo maps to alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported = Alcohol use disorder), whereas PGS000201 is for “Problematic alcohol use” with an alcohol dependence measurement EFO and a DSM-5 criteria count (quantitative/problem-use proxy rather than dependence diagnosis). On PRS evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002739 provides a clinically interpretable risk separation (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, CI 1.32–2.34), which is a stronger discriminative signal than PGS000201’s small incremental ΔR²=0.01192 (and PGS000201’s metric is explicitly vs covariates, making it more packaging-dependent). PGS002739 is also developed from multiple cohorts (MVP/PGC/UKB) and evaluated in AFR, aligning with its study focus, while PGS000201 is UKB-only EUR; despite PGS000201’s larger variant count, the phenotype mismatch and weaker PRS-comparable signal make it less supported for alcohol dependence.

Both candidates map cleanly to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS004913 has better endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported matches alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis directly) whereas PGS001777’s phenotyping_reported is restricted/shifted to “Cirrhosis (males)”. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS001777’s AUROC=0.671 is explicitly a full-model metric and thus not comparable as PRS performance, while PGS004913 at least provides an R²=0.029 and an OR (top vs bottom deciles)=4.4 with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs), avoiding obvious clinical leakage. Structurally, PGS004913 uses more variants (20 vs 3) and has explicit training sample size and multi-cohort development (GenomALC, NIAAA), giving a more supported PRS evidence package than the sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates in PGS001777.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same reported/phenotyped trait (M13 Other arthritis), same EFO mapping (arthritis), same UKB training cohort, identical training (n=174,489) and validation size (n=56,192), and identical EUR-only DEV/EVAL ancestry. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (PGS-only and top-level AUC/R2 are null), and covariates are unknown for both, so performance must be judged mainly by the available effect size and structural signals. PGS004547 has a stronger reported per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.262) than PGS004477 (OR=1.196), and its method (RFDiseasemetaPRS) suggests a multi-score/meta-PRS aggregation, which is a positive structural signal when other fields are tied. Therefore PGS004547 is better supported on the visible evidence.

PGS001344 has cleaner, PRS-comparable performance reporting: it explicitly provides PGS-only AUROC (0.64568) and PGS-only R² (0.05973), enabling a direct PRS quality readout and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS002727 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (AUROC 0.66, R² 0.04) with covariates listed as Unknown, and its endpoint is explicitly pediatric asthma, which is a narrower subtype mismatch versus the generic target “asthma.” While PGS002727 is disease-focused and has a strong per-SD OR (1.57) plus very large validation N, the lack of PGS-only metrics and the pediatric restriction make its PRS evidence less directly comparable than PGS001344’s PRS-only metrics and general doctor-diagnosed asthma endpoint.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis) and have identical covariates and validation ancestry/size (EUR; n=337,910), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either, so metrics don’t separate them beyond similar HRs (PGS002755 HR=1.249 vs PGS004587 HR=1.153). In this no-PGS-only-metrics setting, structural signals dominate: PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is generally better suited to polygenic traits like eczema than PGS004587’s 23 genome-wide significant SNPs. PGS004587’s listed training cohorts are a mild plus, but not enough to outweigh the much stronger genome-wide model structure and slightly stronger HR evidence in PGS002755.

Both candidates map cleanly to asthma (trait_efo=asthma) with acceptable basic covariates, but PGS001344 has clearer PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R2=0.05973, whereas PGS001782 lacks a PGS-only AUROC (only a full-model AUROC=0.659 is shown, which is not comparable per guidance) and provides only a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.048844. Endpoint fidelity is slightly clearer for PGS001344 (“diagnosed by doctor” in phenotyping_reported) versus the more generic “Asthma” for PGS001782. Although PGS001782 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants and multi-biobank GWAS context, the missing PRS-only AUROC and weaker PRS-comparable R2 make it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001344.

PGS004587 is the better-supported choice for the generic target trait “atopic eczema” because its endpoint is closer to the broad disease concept (trait_reported: atopic dermatitis; phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis) and it is evaluated in a large EUR cohort (n=337,910), whereas PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis) and is developed/evaluated in a Canadian multi-ancestry (MAE) context with small validation (n=676), reducing transportability to the typical atopic eczema use case. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 appear to be full-model metrics (and are implausibly high relative to the eczema heritability ceiling), so they cannot be used as clean PRS evidence, while PGS004587 at least reports a modest PRS-stratified HR (1.153 high vs low) without relying on non-comparable full-model discrimination.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUC/C-index is not a reliable cross-model discriminator—especially since PGS005168’s very high C-index (0.8718) is paired with explicit clinical risk-calculator packaging (covariates include CHARGE-AF), a strong negative comparability/leakage signal. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding that packaging concern, and also shows strong PRS effect-size evidence (OR 1.82 per SD with tight CI) plus a stronger structural setup (PRS-CSx with substantially more variants: 1,271,239 vs 382,963). While PGS005168 has broader multi-cohort development and larger EUR validation (52,757 vs 37,161), the CHARGE-AF covariate wrapper makes its reported performance less informative for standalone PRS quality, so PGS005313 is better-supported on cleaner evidence.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not directly comparable as a PRS metric. However, PGS005168’s reported discrimination is explicitly packaged with a named clinical risk calculator covariate (CHARGE-AF) in addition to demographics/array, making its high C-index (0.8718) likely covariate-driven and less informative for standalone PRS quality. PGS002814 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding that risk-wrapper leakage, and it provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.94) as supportive PRS signal. Despite being evaluated only in East Asians (vs EUR for PGS005168), the cleaner covariate design and strong effect size make PGS002814 better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training N (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), same validation N (11,322), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC). With endpoint fidelity and comparability essentially tied, the only visible differentiator is slightly stronger reported performance for PGS000454: marginally higher Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487) and higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.79 vs 3.61) while AUROC is identical (0.632). Given these are full-model/auxiliary metrics and differences are tiny, confidence is low but PGS000454 has the small edge.

PGS002755 is the better-supported standalone PRS for the target trait atopic eczema because it matches the general disease concept (trait_reported: Atopic dermatitis; phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), which is structurally more appropriate for a polygenic disease than PGS001773’s very sparse 25-variant score. PGS001773’s only reported discrimination (AUROC=0.93, R²=0.49) is explicitly full-model/non-PRS-comparable and is likely inflated by covariates including parental ethnicity (family/ancestry packaging), and its endpoint is narrower (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis) than the target. PGS002755 lacks PRS-only AUC/R² too, but it provides a PRS-linked effect size (HR high vs low PRS=1.249) in a much larger European evaluation (n=337,910) with relatively standard covariates, making it the more credible PRS evidence package overall.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training n=11,734, same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation size (n=11,322). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not strong evidence. Given this near-tie, PGS000454 has a marginal edge with slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0489 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456 only slightly leads on top-1% OR (3.95 vs 3.79). Overall support is essentially equivalent, so confidence is low.

Both candidates align to the target (atrial flutter) only as a combined endpoint with atrial fibrillation (same trait_efo), but PGS001339 provides cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R2=0.02447 (and incremental AUROC), which can be sanity-checked against the atrial flutter heritability ceiling and interpreted as PRS signal. PGS002050 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 entirely and only reports partial correlation (partial-r=0.1034), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination ranking. While PGS002050 has a larger variant count and training N, those are secondary to having explicit PRS-only metrics; both are UKB-based framework/portability-style scores with broadly similar basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation. Hence PGS001339 is better supported on the visible fields.

PGS001263 is a direct atrial flutter endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial flutter) and reports clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.025), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling and interpreted without substituting full-model performance. PGS002050 has a broader phenotype (atrial fibrillation and flutter rather than flutter alone) and, critically, lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2; it reports only partial correlation (partial-r=0.1034), making its predictive performance less directly comparable for PRS ranking. Although PGS002050 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many more variants and larger training N, the missing PRS-comparable discrimination metrics and less specific endpoint make it less well-supported for the specific target trait atrial flutter.

PGS001263 is the better-supported match for the target trait (atrial flutter) because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all specifically “Atrial flutter,” whereas PGS001339 targets a broader combined phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) and is additionally framed as time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: “TTE atrial fibrillation and flutter”), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic atrial flutter target. Both are from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical training size, covariates, and validation sample size, so performance and design are the main differentiators; PGS001263 also has slightly higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447), with both remaining plausible under the heritability ceiling. Overall, the direct phenotype fidelity plus marginally stronger PRS-only metrics favors PGS001263.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same method (GWAS Hits), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics with basic covariates). With no PRS-comparable metrics to separate them, the only visible differentiators are small full-model performance/effect-size differences: PGS000452 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0487 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456 has a higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.95 vs 3.61). Given the guidance that small full-model AUROC differences are weak but still the cleanest available tie-break here (covariates are the same and basic), PGS000452 edges out, though the evidence is essentially tied.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and only basic covariates (PGS005313: age, sex; PGS002814: age, sex, 20 PCs), so phenotype/covariate comparability does not separate them much. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.78 vs 0.74) are not clean PRS-comparable and should be discounted. Under the fallback when PRS-only metrics are absent, PGS005313 is better supported structurally and for transportability: it uses a genome-wide cross-ancestry shrinkage approach (PRS-CSx) with far broader variant coverage (1,271,239 vs 4,520) and shows multi-ancestry GWAS input plus multi-ancestry evaluation (European, African, South Asian, East Asian, Hispanic/LatAm, Other), whereas PGS002814 is evaluated only in East Asian. Both show strong per-SD ORs (PGS005313 OR=1.82; PGS002814 OR≈1.94), so effect size does not outweigh PGS005313’s broader, more polygenic model and validation breadth.

PGS000924 has clearer PRS-comparable performance evidence for the target disease axis: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.88697 and PGS-only R2=0.21843 in Europeans, whereas PGS001824 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716) and no PRS-only AUC/R2, making its predictive strength harder to assess. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both, but PGS001824 is a direct bilirubin-excretion disorder while PGS000924 is a combined porphyrin+bilirubin time-to-event phenotype (a mild mismatch/packaging penalty). Both are UKB-based framework-style scores; however, the decisive differentiator here is that PGS000924 provides explicit PRS-only metrics (despite the high R2 being above the provided h2_obs ceiling, which lowers confidence), while PGS001824 lacks comparable PRS-only metrics altogether.

PGS002032 is the better-supported choice for the target trait (bilirubin metabolism disease) because its endpoint is a direct match to the target EFO ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion" mapped to bilirubin metabolism disease) without the added cross-trait composite seen in PGS000924 ("porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism"), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far broader variant coverage (19,768 vs 5), which is structurally more appropriate for polygenic signal capture. Although PGS000924 reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits") and its very high PRS-only R² (0.218) is implausible relative to the provided local heritability ceiling (~0.089), raising comparability/sanity concerns; PGS002032’s reported partial-r (0.0716) is more consistent with that ceiling even though it lacks AUC/R². Both are UKB-derived with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation, but overall PGS002032 has cleaner phenotype focus and fewer red flags in metric plausibility than PGS000924.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion"), same UKB-only training (n=391,124), same covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), same ancestry distribution for development/evaluation, same validation size (n=19,924), and essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs). With metrics and phenotype unable to differentiate, the structural tie-break favors PGS002032 because it is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far broader variant coverage (19,768 variants via LDpred2) versus the extremely sparse 22-variant penalized regression score in PGS001824, which is less likely to capture polygenic signal when all else is equal.

PGS001033 is the better-supported choice for the target umbrella trait “blood coagulation disease” because it directly maps to the target EFO and provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.634 and PGS-only R²=0.0578) with only basic covariates, plus broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS). In contrast, PGS002034 targets a narrower, different EFO concept (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency) and reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0563) with no PRS-only AUROC/R², making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for PRS ranking despite higher variant count and training N.

Both candidates are near-clones: same publication, same SDPR method, similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and both lack PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R2; only a small partial R² reported). Endpoint fidelity to the target trait “bipolar disorder” is weak for both because phenotyping_reported is not a bipolar diagnosis (A: DSM5 depression behavior; B: sluggish cognitive tempo). Given the target is generic bipolar disorder, PGS002787 (bipolar I) is the closer and more clinically canonical bipolar endpoint than PGS002788 (bipolar II), and the tiny partial R² difference (0.00275 vs 0.00307) is not a reliable differentiator; hence PGS002787 narrowly wins on concept alignment despite low confidence.

PGS002786 is the better match to the target trait (bipolar disorder): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly “Bipolar disorder”/“bipolar disorder,” whereas PGS002787 is explicitly subtype-restricted (“Type 1 bipolar disorder” / “bipolar I disorder”), which is a narrower endpoint than the target. Both candidates otherwise look like near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training cohort, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same basic covariates age+PCs1-3, no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, and only tiny partial R² values that are not clearly PRS-only). PGS002787 has a slightly higher partial R² (0.00275 vs 0.00251), but given the endpoint mismatch and that these are full/partial-model metrics tied to non-disease phenotyping fields, that small difference is weak evidence. Hence PGS002786 wins on endpoint fidelity, with low confidence due to both having non-aligned phenotyping_reported and lacking PRS-comparable metrics.

PGS002786 is the better match to the target trait (bipolar disorder): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly bipolar disorder, whereas PGS002788 targets the subtype bipolar II disorder (trait_efo: bipolar II disorder), which is a narrower endpoint mismatch for a generic bipolar disorder target. Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training cohort, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same validation n=2,524, and similarly basic covariates age+PCs1-3) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only metric shown is partial R² from a full model, where PGS002788 is only slightly higher (0.00307 vs 0.00251), a small difference that is not decisive given endpoint fidelity. Therefore the exact endpoint alignment of PGS002786 outweighs the marginal full-model partial R² edge of PGS002788.

Both candidates are essentially matched on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Breast cancer/breast carcinoma), study context (same publication), training cohort and size (UKB; n=12,483), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS) and validation N (n=48,968), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/R² shown, with covariates listed as 0). With metrics largely non-discriminating, PGS004153 has a slight edge via marginally higher reported full-model AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598), R² (0.0764 vs 0.0736), and OR per SD (1.826 vs 1.806), plus a modestly higher variant count (1,133,268 vs 1,041,298). Differences are small, so confidence is low.

PGS001301 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.82867; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.14224) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and includes some non-EUR evaluation (AFR/SAS) alongside EUR. In contrast, PGS000316 only provides a full-model AUROC (0.879) with covariates listed as unknown and no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination less interpretable as PRS performance. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (celiac disease), though PGS000316 is cleaner-labeled while PGS001301 uses a composite ‘Malabsorption/coeliac disease’; overall the availability of PRS-only metrics outweighs the mild phenotype-label broadening.

Both candidates are near-clones for breast carcinoma: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Breast cancer), identical variant count (1,041,298), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (12,483), same ancestry distribution (GWAS/DEV EUR; EVAL EUR+SAS) and same validation N (48,968), with covariates listed as 0 for both. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the only visible metrics are full-model AUROC/R² and effect sizes, which are essentially indistinguishable; however PGS004040 is marginally higher on full-model AUROC (0.65978971 vs 0.65975886), R² (0.07391539 vs 0.07358668), and OR per SD (1.8088 vs 1.8065). Given the tiny differences and overlapping CIs, confidence is low, but PGS004040 has the slight edge on the available performance/effect-size fields.

PGS001033 is the better-supported choice for the broad target “blood coagulation disease” because it maps directly to that EFO term and provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.634 and PGS-only R²=0.0578 with only basic covariates), plus broader multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS). In contrast, PGS001826 targets a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the generic coagulation disease umbrella) and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² entirely, reporting only partial correlation, making its predictive evidence less directly comparable despite more variants and larger training N.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical (same trait_reported, trait_efo, phenotyping_reported), come from the same UKB portability paper, have the same training size, ancestry distribution, covariates, and validation sample size, and show virtually identical PRS-comparable performance (partial-r 0.0563 for PGS002034 vs 0.0562 for PGS001826 with overlapping CIs). With metrics tied, the only meaningful differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally favored for capturing polygenic signal when other evidence is equal. The win is therefore slight and confidence is low due to near-identical observed performance.

PGS001301 has clearly reported PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867 and PGS-only R²=0.14224) with transparent basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and its PRS-only R² is below the provided celiac disease liability h² ceiling (~0.2305), making the signal interpretable. PGS000040 is endpoint-faithful (Coeliac disease) but only reports a full-model AUROC=0.9 with no PGS-only AUROC/R², so its apparent performance cannot be cleanly attributed to the PRS and is not comparable. Although PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a negative archetype signal), the presence of explicit PGS-only metrics and broader evaluation ancestries outweighs PGS000040’s missing PRS-only evidence in this head-to-head.

Both candidates align well to the target trait (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported cervical cancer) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model C-index/AUROC is discounted and effect-size/covariate cleanliness become key. PGS000073 shows slightly stronger/cleaner overall support: it has a higher reported discrimination (C-index ~0.75 vs 0.566 for PGS005165) and a similar per-SD HR (1.22 vs 1.20), with no obvious clinical-risk-calculator packaging in either. While PGS005165 uses more SNPs (15 vs 10) and is EAS-specific (useful if deploying in EAS), its much weaker reported discrimination and similar HR leave it less supported on the visible fields. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, confidence is moderate rather than high.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Breast cancer/breast carcinoma), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training N (12,483), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), validation N (48,968), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/R² are shown, so they are weak differentiators). Given this near-clone context, PGS004153 has a small but consistent edge in the available empirical signals: slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598), higher R² (0.0764 vs 0.0739), and slightly stronger effect sizes (OR per SD 1.826 vs 1.809; β 0.602 vs 0.593). It also uses an ensemble/multi-PRS method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), which is a positive structural signal over the single-score LDpred2.CV sibling (PGS004040) when other fields are otherwise matched.

Both candidates are endpoint-identical for cholelithiasis (ICD10 K80), from the same publication, with the same training cohort (UKB), training N (174,489), validation N (56,192), EUR-only development/evaluation, and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only OR reported). With metrics otherwise missing, the main differentiator is the reported per-SD effect size: PGS004546 has a higher OR (1.2986) than PGS004476 (1.2194), indicating stronger PRS signal on the visible record. Method differences (RFDiseasemetaPRS vs LDpred2) are secondary here because these are same-study siblings and no PRS-only AUC/R2 is provided to corroborate method-based expectations.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident cervical cancer; EUR evaluation). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model AUROC/C-index in PGS000073 (0.745–0.75 vs 0.613) is not a clean PRS comparison, especially given PGS000073’s much heavier covariate set (PCs, parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years, array) versus the lighter age+smoking adjustment in PGS003428. Structurally, PGS003428 is a disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis-derived genome-wide LDpred score with ~2.9M variants and a stronger per-SD HR (1.33 vs 1.22), whereas PGS000073 is a sparse 10-variant genome-wide-significant score from a cross-cancer evaluation framework. Given missing PRS-only metrics, the cleaner covariates + stronger effect size + more polygenic construction and disease-focused development make PGS003428 better-supported overall.

Both candidates match the target trait well at the concept level (trait_reported/trait_efo = asthma). However, PGS001782 has cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 of 0.048844 (and AUROC 0.659), which is interpretable as PRS signal and is below the asthma heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0077; liability h2≈0.1515). In contrast, PGS002727 only provides full-model metrics (AUROC 0.66, R2 0.04) with no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination evidence less comparable for PRS ranking despite a strong OR per SD (1.57). PGS002727’s pediatric-only phenotyping_reported ('Pediatric asthma') is also a narrower endpoint than the generic asthma target, whereas PGS001782 uses a generic 'Asthma' phenotype with basic covariates (sex, age, PCs) and a large multi-biobank development context.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coeliac disease) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.879 for PGS000316 vs 0.90 for PGS000040) are not cleanly comparable PRS metrics. With performance evidence essentially tied/unclean, structural signals favor PGS000040: it uses many more variants (228 vs 53), consistent with capturing more polygenic signal, and has fully EUR development/evaluation ancestry alignment. PGS000316’s much larger validation sample size is a weak tie-breaker and its mixed/NR ancestry reporting plus reliance on full-model AUROC doesn’t provide clearer PRS-only support. Overall, PGS000040 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target trait well at the concept level (trait_efo=chronic kidney disease; stage ≥3 wording is near-synonymous). However, PGS002237 has clearer endpoint fidelity via an explicit phenotyping definition (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2, i.e., stage 3b+), and it shows broader evaluation across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE) rather than the AFR-only development/evaluation of PGS005090, which limits generalizability when deployment ancestry is unspecified. On performance, neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable; moreover PGS002237’s stronger per-SD OR (1.47 vs 1.41) is modestly better PRS signal. PGS005090’s higher full-model AUROC (0.90) and larger validation N are discounted because they are not PRS-only metrics and validation size is a weak tie-breaker.

PGS002237 has tighter endpoint fidelity to CKD as a clinical severity definition (stage 3+; eGFR <45), and it comes from a CKD-focused cross-ancestry prediction study with explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE). It also shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.47) than PGS004158 (OR 1.39), which is meaningful given that neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R² (both only show full-model metrics, which are not comparable PRS measures). PGS004158’s phenotype (“CKD or dialysis”) is broader/less specific and its reported AUROC (~0.59) is weak and still full-model; while its covariates are cleaner (“0”), that doesn’t outweigh the stronger endpoint specificity and effect-size evidence plus broader ancestry evaluation support in PGS002237.

Both candidates target the same COPD endpoint with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported and come from the same publication and method family (PRS-CS-auto) with EUR-only evaluation, so endpoint fidelity and study archetype do not differentiate them. The clearest PRS-comparable metric is the covariates-regressed-out (PGS-only) Nagelkerke R2: PGS001783 reports substantially higher PGS-only R2 (0.038092) than PGS001788 (0.0163), and it also has a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.74 vs 0.715), though full-model AUROC is secondary. PGS001788’s much larger validation N and slightly higher variant count are weaker tie-break signals and do not outweigh the materially stronger PRS-only R2 for PGS001783.

PGS001174 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R2=0.028 (and incremental AUROC), allowing a clean PRS assessment and a heritability sanity check (PGS-only R2 is plausible relative to the provided h2_obs≈0.021). It also has basic, non-leaky covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004476 has strong endpoint fidelity (ICD10 K80) and a genome-wide LDpred2 build with many variants, but it provides no AUROC/R2 at all and only a modest per-SD OR≈1.22 plus unknown covariates, making its standalone PRS performance and comparability much less evidenced from the visible fields.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo cervical carcinoma; trait_reported cervical cancer). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model C-index is only weakly informative; still, PGS003428 shows stronger discrimination evidence (C-index 0.613 vs 0.566) and a stronger per-SD effect size (HR 1.33 vs 1.20). Structurally, PGS003428 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred) with ~2.9M variants, which is generally better for polygenic signal capture than PGS005165’s 15 genome-wide significant loci. Covariates are not heavily leakage-prone in either (age+smoking vs age/region/PCs). PGS005165’s main advantage is East Asian evaluation (useful for EAS deployment), but on visible PRS-strength evidence PGS003428 is better supported overall.

PGS001174 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance and transparency: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R²=0.028 (and incremental AUROC), with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array). Its PGS-only R² is also plausible relative to the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.021) as a sanity check signal rather than an obvious inflation artifact. In contrast, PGS004546 has no AUROC/R² at all (only an OR=1.30 of moderate strength) and lists covariates as unknown, making its predictive quality and comparability harder to judge despite an ICD10-aligned endpoint (K80) and large variant count. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both map to cholelithiasis), but the lack of PRS-comparable metrics in PGS004546 leaves weaker visible support than PGS001174.

PGS001783 is the better-supported standalone COPD PRS on the visible fields because it reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out / PGS-only R2 = 0.038092), which is interpretable and passes the heritability sanity check (below h2_liability≈0.0388). It also uses only basic covariates (sex, age, PCs) and is developed in a broad multi-biobank context, reducing single-cohort optimism risk. In contrast, PGS004536 is framed as an integrated risk-factor + disease metaPRS (RFDiseasemetaPRS), with covariates listed as Unknown and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported; it provides only an OR (1.4876, moderate) and is developed solely in UKB, making its evidence package less clean/comparable for a pure COPD PRS despite similar endpoint mapping (J44 COPD subtype) and larger validation N.

PGS000726 is the better-supported match to the target trait (cirrhosis of liver): its trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are generic “Cirrhosis/cirrhosis of liver,” aligning directly with the umbrella endpoint, whereas PGS000704 is explicitly restricted to “Alcoholic cirrhosis” (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), a narrower subtype mismatch for a generic cirrhosis target. Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS000704’s reported 0.711 C-index is a full-model metric and not comparable as standalone PRS evidence; its per-SD HR (1.18) is also weaker than PGS000726’s per-SD OR (1.32) and top-vs-bottom quintile OR (2.26). Additionally, PGS000726 comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort cirrhosis genetics study with multiple development cohorts and multi-ancestry evaluation, while PGS000704 is a single-UKB framework-style score (biomarkers paper) with less endpoint-focused support.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are cirrhosis/cirrhosis of liver) and neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC cannot be used as a comparable PRS metric. Given that, structural/study-design signals dominate: PGS004621 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and is developed/validated across a large multi-cohort biobank set with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and very large EUR evaluation (n=1,153,995). PGS000726 is a sparse 12-variant GWAS-hits score; while it reports a strong extreme-quantile OR (top 20% vs bottom 20% OR=2.26), it lacks comparable discrimination metrics and has much smaller validation (n=30,469) with mixed/partly NR evaluation ancestry. Overall, the genome-wide, multi-cohort design of PGS004621 is better-supported for a polygenic disease endpoint than the very sparse PGS000726, despite both lacking PRS-only AUC/R2.

Both candidates are well-aligned to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Coronary artery disease”) and both use only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so we must lean on effect sizes and transportability signals. PGS003725 shows materially stronger PRS discrimination evidence via effect sizes (OR 2.14 per SD and HR 1.75) versus PGS002244’s OR 1.64, and it is explicitly a CAD-focused multi-ancestry PRS paper with broad multi-ancestry evaluation listed. PGS002244 has more variants and slightly larger training/validation Ns, but those are weaker differentiators here given missing PRS-only metrics and similar endpoint/covariate cleanliness. Net: stronger effect-size evidence favors PGS003725.

PGS005090 is better supported for the target trait CKD because its endpoint is more specific and clinically anchored ("Chronic kidney disease (stage 3 or higher)" with phenotyping_reported "Chronic kidney disease") and it comes from a CKD-focused study in Black American populations with multi-cohort development (MVP, REGARDS) and AFR-only evaluation, reducing framework/portability concerns. Although it reports only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.9, R² 0.1) that are not PRS-comparable and likely covariate-influenced (age, sex, diabetes, PCs), it at least provides an OR per SD (1.41) as PRS signal. PGS004158 has a broadly aligned CKD label but a less clean phenotype definition ("Chronic kidney disease or dialysis"), is from a multi-biobank methods evaluation/ensemble framework context, and its reported AUROC/R² are also full-model (not PGS-only) with unclear comparability; its effect size (OR ~1.39) is similar, so it doesn’t outweigh the stronger endpoint fidelity and disease-focused multi-cohort context of PGS005090.

Both candidates match the target CAD endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coronary artery disease) and use only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs; PGS000013 also adds chip), so phenotype fidelity and leakage risk are similar. The key difference is evidence of PRS signal and transportability: PGS003725 reports strong per-SD effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14), which is direct PRS discrimination evidence, and it is explicitly a multi-ancestry CAD-focused score with broad evaluation ancestries listed. PGS000013 provides a PRS-only R2=0.04 (below the heritability ceiling, so plausible) but its prominent AUROC=0.81 is full-model and not PRS-comparable; it lacks comparable PRS-only AUC and offers no effect sizes here. Given the stronger PRS-specific effect-size evidence plus multi-ancestry evaluation context, PGS003725 is better supported overall despite missing explicit PRS-only R2/AUC.

Both candidates align to COPD (trait_efo matches; PGS004536 uses ICD-10 J44 subtype wording but still COPD-relevant). However, PGS001788 provides a clear PRS-comparable performance metric (pgs_only_r2/Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.0163), which is interpretable and below the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0122; close but not wildly implausible given scale differences), whereas PGS004536 reports no PRS-only AUC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.49). PGS001788 also discloses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and has much broader multi-cohort GWAS development context, while PGS004536 has unknown covariates and UKB-only development. Despite the framework-paper origin of PGS001788 being a mild negative, the presence of an explicit PRS-only R2 and transparent basic adjustment makes it better-supported on the visible fields than PGS004536’s metric-sparse record.

PGS001331 is the better-supported Crohn’s disease PRS because it matches the generic disease endpoint more directly (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are plain “Crohn’s disease”), whereas PGS001330 is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) formulation (“regional enteritis (time-to-event)”), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic Crohn’s disease target. Both are from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical training size (n=269,704), similar covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and the same validation size (n=24,905), so performance and endpoint details drive the decision. On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001331 is slightly stronger (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) and both remain below the heritability ceiling, making PGS001331 the cleaner and marginally better-performing choice.

Both candidates match the target CAD endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coronary artery disease) and use similar basic covariates without obvious clinical-risk packaging. The key difference is evidence strength: PGS002244 provides a strong PRS-discrimination signal via an OR=1.64 per SD (CI 1.61–1.67), whereas PGS000013’s only PRS-comparable metric is a modest PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.04 and its AUROC=0.81 is a full-model metric (not PRS-only) and thus not comparable for PRS ranking. PGS002244 also has larger training (175,364 vs 120,280) and slightly larger validation (343,676 vs 288,978), though these are secondary. Confidence is Moderate because PGS002244 lacks explicit PRS-only AUC/R2, but its strong effect-size evidence outweighs PGS000013’s limited PRS-only R2 and non-comparable full-model AUROC.

PGS004621 is the better-supported match to the target trait (cirrhosis of liver): its trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all generic “Cirrhosis/cirrhosis of liver,” whereas PGS000704 is explicitly restricted to “Alcoholic cirrhosis” (trait_efo alcoholic liver cirrhosis), a subtype mismatch for the broader target. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (both only show full-model discrimination), so the small full-model difference (0.68 vs 0.711 C-index) is not a reliable PRS comparator; in that setting, PGS004621’s stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.42 vs HR 1.18 for PGS000704) and its disease-focused multi-cohort development context (multiple biobanks vs UKB-only) provide better support than PGS000704’s framework-like single-biobank origin despite its slightly higher full-model metric and multi-ancestry evaluation.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported all-cause dementia; trait_efo dementia), but PGS005170 has stronger structural and transportability support: it is an integrative ensemble of 24 component PRSs with genome-wide coverage (1,320,229 variants) and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR), whereas PGS004281 is a very sparse 110-variant UKB-only GenoBoost score evaluated only in EUR. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model AUROC for PGS004281 (0.819 vs 0.761) is not a clean PRS-comparable advantage; additionally PGS005170 provides an HR per SD (1.25) giving at least some PRS-specific signal. PGS005170’s covariates include APOE ε2/ε4 dosage (a potential comparability concern), but overall the ensemble design plus broader evaluation context outweigh PGS004281’s single-cohort, sparse construction with only full-model metrics.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to Crohn’s disease (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match). However, PGS001331 is from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) using a very sparse snpnet model (257 variants), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly despite having explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.579, PGS-only R2 0.00677). PGS004254 is a genome-wide shrinkage score (LDpred2-auto; 744,682 variants) with basic covariates and reports a strong effect size (OR 2.18), which is meaningful PRS evidence even though only a full-model AUROC (0.72) is shown and cannot be treated as PRS-only. Given the framework penalty and weak PRS-only performance for PGS001331 versus the stronger structural properties and effect-size support for PGS004254, PGS004254 is better-supported overall.

PGS002759 is better supported for the target trait because it has tighter endpoint fidelity (trait_efo = major depressive disorder, a specific depressive disorder subtype) and provides a direct PRS effect size in validation (OR per SD = 1.26, 95% CI 1.22–1.30), whereas PGS002036 reports only a weak partial correlation (partial-r = 0.0556) and no OR/HR/AUC/R2. Although PGS002036 has broader multi-ancestry evaluation and a defined UKB training sample, it comes from a UKB portability framework paper and lacks a clear, PRS-comparable discrimination metric; PGS002759’s explicit OR offers cleaner evidence of PRS signal for depression/MDD in Europeans.

PGS004254 is the better-supported Crohn’s disease PRS on endpoint fidelity and structural plausibility: it targets a direct Crohn’s disease diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both Crohn’s disease) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto) with very large variant coverage (744,682), which is generally more appropriate for a polygenic autoimmune disease than a very sparse model. Although PGS004254 lacks PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R2; the visible AUROC=0.72 appears to be full-model and thus not directly comparable), it does report a strong effect size (OR 2.18) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). In contrast, PGS001330 comes from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with only 220 variants and a time-to-event phenotype, and its PRS-only performance is explicitly modest (PGS-only AUROC 0.57593; PGS-only R2 0.00621), despite broader evaluation ancestries. Given the framework penalty plus weaker PRS-only metrics for PGS001330, PGS004254 is preferred even with missing PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS004281 is the better match to the target trait dementia on endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all explicitly “All-cause dementia/dementia,” whereas PGS000823 is labeled/trained as Alzheimer’s disease (trait_efo Alzheimer disease) with phenotyping_reported “Incident all-cause dementia,” creating a mixed AD vs dementia alignment. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS004281 at least provides a single, clearly described validation record with basic covariates (age, sex, PC1-10) and a large UKB-based development sample; its reported AUROC is full-model and thus discounted, yet it is not obviously driven by heavy clinical leakage. PGS000823 lacks comparable discrimination metrics entirely (only an HR top-tertile contrast of 1.36) and has no training sample size reported, making its support weaker despite multi-cohort provenance. Overall, the exact dementia endpoint coherence of PGS004281 outweighs the limited effect-size-only evidence in PGS000823.

PGS005170 is the better-supported match to the target trait dementia because its reported trait and EFO mapping are directly aligned to dementia ("All-cause dementia", trait_efo="dementia") with the same incident all-cause dementia phenotyping as PGS000823, while also using a much stronger structural approach (integrative ensemble of 24 component PRSs with genome-wide methods; 1,320,229 variants) versus PGS000823’s very sparse 23 genome-wide-significant-variant score for Alzheimer’s disease (trait_efo="Alzheimer disease"), which is a narrower concept than all-cause dementia. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS005170 at least provides an HR per SD (1.25) and a full-model AUROC (0.761) with mostly standard covariates plus APOE genotype; PGS000823 provides only a tertile HR (1.36 top vs bottom) with minimal covariates, which is less directly comparable as a PRS strength signal. Although PGS000823 has a much larger validation sample (12,978 vs 2,032), validation N is a weak tie-breaker and does not outweigh PGS005170’s superior endpoint alignment to dementia and substantially stronger genome-wide/ensemble construction.

Both candidates align well to the target depressive disorder (both map to EFO major depressive disorder; A is explicitly Major Depressive Disorder and B is Depression with matching EFO). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so comparable PRS metrics are largely missing. PGS002759 provides a directly interpretable PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.26, 95% CI 1.22–1.30) with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), giving cleaner, PRS-relevant performance evidence than PGS003333, which only reports a full-model Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.022 and has covariates listed as unknown (making the R2 harder to interpret as PRS-driven). Ancestry and variant counts are essentially the same (EUR-only; ~1.09M variants), and validation N is similar, so the effect-size evidence and covariate clarity tip the balance to PGS002759.

PGS003333 has tighter endpoint fidelity to the target depressive disorder via an explicit Major Depressive Disorder phenotype (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both MDD), whereas PGS002036 is a broader “Depression” label coming from a UKB portability framework paper. Both lack clean PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS003333 at least reports an interpretable pseudo-R2 (0.022) while PGS002036 reports only a partial correlation (0.0556), making performance evidence similarly limited but slightly clearer for PGS003333. PGS002036’s multi-ancestry evaluation is a plus, yet given the stronger phenotype specificity of PGS003333 and no decisive PRS-only metric advantage for PGS002036, PGS003333 is marginally better supported overall.

PGS003576 is better supported for the target “depressive disorder” because its endpoint is explicitly Major Depressive Disorder (lifetime) with phenotyping_reported “Major depressive disorder,” tightly aligned to the target and EFO mapping, and it shows broader external evaluation across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/ASN/EAS/EUR) with a stated training cohort (UKB) and training N=67,164. Although its only reported metric is an R²=0.0241 that appears to be full-model (not PRS-only), PGS002759 also lacks PRS-only AUC/R² and provides only a moderate OR per SD (1.26) plus missing training sample/cohort details; it is also from a broader “family history and polygenic risk across 24 common diseases” framework-style paper, which is generally weaker evidence than a disease-focused MDD study when PRS-only metrics are absent. Overall, PGS003576 has stronger phenotype fidelity and more robust validation context than PGS002759.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same Nat Genet study, same method (PRS-CS), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same phenotyping_reported (Dilated cardiomyopathy), same covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), and same validation sample size (n=347,585), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics), so performance evidence is limited and largely comparable. PGS004862 is preferred because it is explicitly the MTAG-enhanced version (trait_reported: "Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)"), which domain guidance treats as a legitimate power-boost and mildly preferred over the base trait, and it also shows slightly stronger reported full-model metrics and effect size (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048; OR 1.76 vs 1.56) than PGS004861. Confidence is moderate because the metric differences are small and not PRS-only.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo=major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported is MDD in both), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (both only show small full-model/unspecified R² ~0.02, which is not cleanly comparable as PRS-only). Given that, structural/transportability evidence breaks the tie: PGS003576 has explicit basic covariates (PCs 1–10) and, importantly, much broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/AMR/ASN/EAS/EUR across 10 records) versus PGS003333 being EUR-only for both GWAS and evaluation. PGS003576 also has substantially higher variant count (5.8M vs 1.1M), which is a supportive structural signal when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS003333’s multi-cohort training (23andMe/PGC/UKB) is a plus, but with unknown covariates and EUR-only evaluation it is less supported for general depressive disorder use than PGS003576’s broader validation context.

PGS002036 is the better-supported choice for the target trait “depressive disorder” because its endpoint alignment is closer (trait_efo exactly “depressive disorder” and phenotyping_reported “Depression”) whereas PGS003576 targets the narrower/adjacent concept “major depressive disorder” (trait_efo “major depressive disorder”, phenotyping_reported “Major depressive disorder”). Neither record provides clean PRS-only AUC/R²; PGS003576 reports only an undifferentiated R²=0.0241 (likely full-model/unclear), while PGS002036 reports a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0556), so performance evidence is weak and not decisively comparable for either. With metrics near-tied in interpretability, PGS002036’s stronger phenotype/EFO match plus its broader stated evaluation ancestry mix (including AFR/EAS/SAS/GME alongside EUR) outweigh PGS003576’s larger variant count and larger validation N.

PGS004951 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides explicit PRS-comparable performance (univariate/PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI and delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004861 reports only full-model metrics (AUROC=0.70, R²=0.048) that are not comparable as standalone PRS evidence. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004951’s “(MTAG)” is not a phenotype mismatch and its phenotyping is explicitly clinical DCM). Structurally, both use PRS-CS, but PGS004951 has higher variant count (1,075,760 vs 713,932) and a stronger effect size (OR 1.93 vs 1.56). Although PGS004861 has a much larger validation sample (347,585 vs 7,761) and includes age/sex covariates, the lack of PRS-only metrics makes its apparent AUROC advantage non-informative for PRS quality compared with PGS004951’s direct PRS-only reporting.

Both candidates align well to the target (same trait_efo Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is a direct Dupuytren/palmar fascia contracture endpoint in both). PGS001254 has clearly reported PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6646 and PGS-only R² 0.0247), whereas PGS002092 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r 0.0797) and has no PRS-only AUC/R², making its predictive strength harder to judge. Although PGS002092 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with many variants and includes multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of standard PRS-only discrimination metrics on the visible record leaves weaker direct evidence than PGS001254’s explicit PGS-only AUROC/R².

PGS000997 is better supported for the target trait (diverticular disease) because it has clearer endpoint alignment to the EFO term via an explicit diagnosis label (“Diverticular disease of intestine”) and reports materially stronger PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 and PGS-only R² 0.0178) than PGS000996 (PGS-only AUROC 0.552; R² 0.0037), with the same basic covariates and same pan-trait UKB framework context. Although PGS000996 has a larger validation sample (67,425 vs 24,905) and includes diverticulitis in the reported trait, its weaker PRS-only metrics and much smaller variant set (368 vs 5,757) make it less convincing overall; both scores’ PRS-only R² remain below the trait heritability ceiling, so the higher R² in PGS000997 is plausible rather than inflated.

PGS001792 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209, which is directly comparable and stays below the glaucoma heritability ceiling noted in the context. PGS004944 lacks any PRS-only AUC/R2 and only shows a full-model AUROC (0.748) plus an OR=1.74, making its discrimination evidence less cleanly comparable. Endpoint fidelity is similar (both target primary open-angle glaucoma), but PGS004944’s phenotyping is explicitly self-reported, while PGS001792’s is not flagged as self-report. Although PGS004944 has slightly larger validation N and more performance records, those are weak tie-breakers versus having an explicit PRS-only R2.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to dupuytren contracture (same EFO; phenotyping_reported matches the disease concept). PGS001254 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.6646 and PGS-only R²=0.0247 (no covariates), whereas PGS001880 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0783) and has no PRS-only AUROC/R², making its predictive strength harder to judge. PGS001880 does have broader multi-ancestry evaluation and a much larger variant set (2443 vs 11), but given the absence of PRS-comparable metrics on its record, the cleaner, directly comparable PGS-only discrimination evidence in PGS001254 outweighs those structural/portability signals.

PGS004614 is the better-supported choice for the target trait (diverticular disease) because it is disease-focused with exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Diverticular disease”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (SBayesR) with very large variant coverage (1,082,282), plus multi-ancestry evaluation is indicated (AFR/EUR/SAS). Although it only reports a full-model AUROC (0.76) and lacks PRS-only metrics, its study context is explicitly diverticular-disease–focused. In contrast, PGS000996 comes from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”), uses a very sparse model (368 variants, snpnet), and while it does report PRS-only metrics, they are weak (PGS-only AUROC 0.5519; PGS R2 0.00372) and the higher AUROC shown in classification_metrics (0.6756) is full-model and not PRS-comparable. Given the framework penalty and weak PRS-only performance for PGS000996, PGS004614 is preferred despite missing PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS000997 is better-supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.591 and PGS R2(no covariates)=0.0178), enabling a clean comparison and a heritability-ceiling sanity check, whereas PGS004614 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.76) with covariates including family history, making the discrimination largely non-comparable to standalone PRS performance and leaving PRS-only performance missing. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (diverticular disease), though PGS000997 is time-to-event; however, PGS004614’s covariate packaging (family history) is a stronger comparability concern than the TTE framing. Despite PGS004614 being disease-focused and genome-wide, the lack of PRS-only metrics plus family-history-adjusted AUROC makes its support weaker than PGS000997’s explicit PRS-only validation.

Both candidates target the same trait (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG); EFO: dilated cardiomyopathy) and use the same method (PRS-CS) with broadly comparable, non-leaky covariates (A: age/sex/PCs; B: sex/PCs). The key differentiator is that PGS004951 reports PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit univariate PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI and delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004862 provides only full-model AUROC/R² (0.71/0.05) which is not a valid substitute for PRS-only metrics. PGS004951 also has a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.93 vs 1.76) and larger variant count (1,075,760 vs 709,534), supporting stronger PRS signal. Although PGS004862 has a much larger validation sample (n=347,585 vs 7,761), validation N is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the lack of PRS-only metrics in A.

PGS001792 is better supported as a standalone PRS for glaucoma because it reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out / PGS-only R2 = 0.03209), which is interpretable against the glaucoma heritability ceiling and provides direct evidence of PRS contribution. It also uses only basic demographic/PC covariates (age/sex terms + PCs), avoiding explicit clinical leakage. In contrast, PGS000137 provides no PGS-only AUC/R2 (only a full-model AUROC=0.8), and its covariates include self-reported family history, making the reported AUROC less comparable to PRS-only performance. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both effectively POAG-aligned), so the cleaner PRS-only metric evidence and covariate design favor PGS001792 despite its framework-style publication context.

Both candidates are essentially matched on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported for Dupuytren contracture), study context (same UKB portability paper), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation sample size (n=18,971). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; both only provide a very similar partial correlation (PGS002092 partial-r=0.0797 vs PGS001880 partial-r=0.0783), so performance evidence is near-tied. With metrics not differentiating, the main visible structural edge is that PGS002092 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (484,484 vs 2,443), which is generally favored for polygenic traits when other fields are equal. The advantage is small given the near-identical partial-r, hence low confidence.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target follicular lymphoma: same trait_efo (follicular lymphoma), same reported/phenotyping label (“Nodular lymphoma”), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; the small full-model AUROC difference (0.538 for PGS000644 vs 0.532 for PGS000643) is weak but is the only direct discrimination signal available under comparable covariates. Effect sizes are also slightly stronger for PGS000644 (OR per SD 1.149 vs 1.133). PGS000643 has a higher top-1% vs rest OR, but given wide CIs and otherwise similar evidence, PGS000644 is marginally better supported overall.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Gout/gout”). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence: PGS001789 reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.031208, which is directly comparable and sits below the gout liability h2 ceiling (~0.0525), making it interpretable as genuine PRS signal. In contrast, PGS004160 provides only full-model AUROC (0.694) and full-model R² (0.089) with no PGS-only metrics, so its performance is not comparable for PRS ranking despite reporting OR/β. Study/transportability also favors PGS001789: it is developed across many biobanks with multi-ancestry GWAS input and broad evaluation, whereas PGS004160 is UKB-only development (EUR) with smaller stated training n=6,704 and limited evaluation ancestries. Therefore PGS001789 is better-supported on the visible PRS-quality fields.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Gout”), come from the same publication, have identical training cohort (UKB), training N (6,704), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), validation N (90,274), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC/R² are not ideal comparators). Given this near-clone context, PGS004160 is better supported because it shows consistently stronger reported performance in the selected European validation record (AUROC 0.6936 vs 0.6851; R² 0.0893 vs 0.0801) and slightly stronger effect sizes (OR 2.05 vs 2.00; β 0.717 vs 0.693), with a higher variant count (976,174 vs 865,644) and an ensemble MultiPRS method that is structurally favored over a single-score LDpred2 sibling when other fields are matched.

PGS000644 is better supported structurally for follicular lymphoma risk: although its trait_reported/phenotyping_reported say “Nodular lymphoma,” its trait_efo maps to follicular lymphoma and “follicular [nodular]” is a close endpoint family match. It uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (lassosum) with ~2.2M variants and reports PRS effect sizes (OR per SD 1.149, CI given) with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), which are low-leakage. In contrast, PGS002304 has perfect label/phenotyping alignment (“Follicular lymphoma”) but is only 6 genome-wide significant variants with no training sample reported, unknown covariates, and no PRS-isolated metrics/effect sizes; its higher reported AUROC (0.61 vs 0.538) is a full-model metric and not PRS-comparable, so it cannot outweigh the much stronger genome-wide PRS evidence package in PGS000644.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Gout/gout”). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence and study/transport context: PGS001789 reports a PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.031208) and is developed across many biobanks with multi-ancestry GWAS input and large validation (n=359,345), with only basic demographic/PC covariates—making its reported PRS signal interpretable.
