PGS004047 does not report any PGS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC and a generic R² alongside covariates listed as “0”), so its performance is less comparable for PRS ranking despite reporting OR/β; it is also trained only in UKB with a small stated training n=6,704 and narrower development ancestry (EUR-only). Therefore PGS001789 is better-supported on visible PRS-relevant evidence.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target (trait_efo=Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis; same method PRSCS; same evaluation ancestry set and validation n=94,651) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative. With endpoints and covariates both effectively indistinguishable (covariates unknown for both), PGS005271 has stronger supportive performance/effect evidence: higher reported AUROC (0.6297 vs 0.6054) and a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.55 vs 1.42; higher beta). Variant count and cohort lists are essentially the same and not decisive. Therefore PGS005271 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_efo Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis) from the same publication family, with identical evaluation ancestry mix and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With performance metrics essentially non-comparable, structural/effect-size evidence dominates: PGS005271 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRSCS) with 1,085,156 variants and shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) than PGS005270’s very weak effect (OR≈1.04) despite PGS005270’s slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630). Given the domain guidance to discount small full-model AUROC differences and prefer stronger PRS signal/structure when PRS-only metrics are missing, PGS005271 is better supported.

PGS004944 is better supported for the target glaucoma because its endpoint is tightly aligned to the clinically dominant subtype (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both primary open-angle glaucoma; trait_efo open-angle glaucoma) and it shows cleaner covariates (age/age^2/sex/ancestry only) plus a strong PRS effect size (OR 1.74 per SD). It also has much broader evaluation context (selected_validation_ancestry spans African unspecified, Hispanic/Latin American, East Asian, South Asian, European; eval MAE 100%) and very large validation sample size (n=407,667), supporting transportability. In contrast, PGS000137 has a broader trait label (glaucoma) but phenotyping is still POAG, and its reported AUROC=0.8 is only a full-model metric with explicit family history in covariates, making the performance less comparable to PRS-only; it also relies on a sparse C+T score (2,673 variants) with narrower development (EUR-only GWAS/DEV). Neither reports PGS-only AUC/R2, so the decision rests on endpoint fidelity, covariate cleanliness, effect-size evidence, and ancestry/validation breadth—favoring PGS004944.

PGS002304 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity to the target: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both explicitly “Follicular lymphoma,” matching the target trait directly. In contrast, PGS000643 is labeled and phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” (despite trait_efo mapping to follicular lymphoma), creating an endpoint/phenotype mismatch that is penalized relative to a direct diagnosis label. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.61 for PGS002304 vs 0.532 for PGS000643) are not strong comparable PRS evidence; however, PGS000643’s additional metrics (Nagelkerke R², ORs) are still tied to a potentially mismatched phenotype. Given the domain guidance prioritizing phenotyping_reported alignment over method/variant count, the direct follicular lymphoma model (PGS002304) is better supported overall, though confidence is moderated by missing PRS-only metrics and unknown covariates for PGS002304.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported is the same “lymphocytic thyroiditis”), come from the same publication family, have the same evaluation ancestry mix (MAE 100%) and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, with covariates unknown), so full-model AUROC differences (0.639 in PGS005270 vs 0.605 in PGS005272) are not a clean differentiator. In this no-PRS-only-metrics setting, structural and effect-size evidence matter more: PGS005272 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRSCS) with ~1,085,142 variants and shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.42) than PGS005270’s sparse P+T 55-variant score with OR≈1.04, indicating materially stronger PRS signal. Therefore PGS005272 is better supported overall despite the slightly lower full-model AUROC.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait heart failure: identical CHF PheCode 428.1 endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported match), same covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same development cohort (MVP), same ancestry distributions, and same validation size (n=31,804). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index (~0.754) is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator and the tiny difference is essentially noise. As a tie-break, PGS005083 has a marginally higher reported effect size (OR 1.455 vs 1.452) and slightly higher full-model C-index (0.75368 vs 0.75358) than PGS005077, so it is very slightly better supported on the visible metrics.

PGS005097 is the better-supported match to the target trait (heart failure): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly heart failure and it is built in a clearly disease-focused, multi-cohort setting (BBJ, BioMe, CKB, FinnGen, GBMI, HERMES, MVP, etc.), which is a strong robustness/transportability signal versus PGS005083 coming from a methods/portability comparison paper with development listed only as MVP. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the slightly higher full-model C-index for PGS005083 (0.754 vs AUROC 0.72) is not a reliable PRS-comparable differentiator, especially given different covariate sets (PGS005083 uses 20 PCs vs 5 PCs). PGS005083 does report an OR per SD (1.455), which is helpful, but it targets a narrower phecode-defined CHF NOS endpoint rather than the broader heart failure concept; overall the endpoint alignment plus multi-cohort disease-architecture context favors PGS005097.

Both candidates are near-clones: same CHF PheCode 428.1 endpoint (good match to heart failure), same EFO, same phenotyping, same method (LDpred), same variant count, same cohorts (MVP), same covariates (age/sex/20 PCs; no major leakage), same ancestry distribution, and same validation N. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index is only a weak differentiator. Given that, PGS005077 edges PGS005076 by slightly stronger reported performance/effect size (C-index 0.7536 vs 0.7532; OR 1.452 vs 1.443), but the differences are tiny, hence low confidence.

PGS005097 is the better-supported match to the target trait (heart failure): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly “Heart failure,” whereas PGS005076 targets “Congestive heart failure (CHF), NOS (PheCode 428.1),” a narrower/administrative phecode instantiation. Neither record provides PRS-comparable performance (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are null for both), so the higher full-model C-index in PGS005076 (0.753 vs 0.72) is not a clean PRS differentiator—especially given different covariate sets (PGS005076 uses 20 PCs vs 5 PCs in PGS005097). On study/transportability evidence, PGS005097 comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort heart-failure genetics paper with many development cohorts (BBJ, BioMe, CKB, FinnGen, GBMI, HERMES, MVP, etc.) and a large validation (n=40,989), while PGS005076 is from a methods-comparison paper with development listed only as MVP and smaller validation (n=31,804). Overall, endpoint fidelity plus stronger disease-focused multi-cohort support favors PGS005097.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: Hodgkin's disease; trait_efo: Hodgkins lymphoma), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort and size (MGI; n=736), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation size (n=775), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics). Given this near-clone setup, PGS000639 is better supported by consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence in the selected validation record: higher AUROC (0.62 vs 0.601), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0276 vs 0.0193), higher OR per SD (1.476 vs 1.377), and higher top-1% vs rest OR (2.64 vs 1.62). With covariates being basic and matched, these differences—while modest—favor PGS000639 over PGS000638.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target hyperthyroidism via the clinically dominant subtype Graves’ disease: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same method (PRSCS), same evaluation ancestry mix (MAE 100%) and same validation sample size (n=94,651), with covariates unknown in both. With no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (only full-model AUROC, which is not PRS-comparable), the only differentiators are small performance/effect-size edges: PGS005265 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.6652 vs 0.6637), higher OR per SD (1.63 vs 1.54) and higher beta (0.486 vs 0.434), plus a trivially higher variant count. These are modest differences, so confidence is low, but they favor PGS005265.

PGS002728 is better supported for the target trait because its endpoint is a clear hip-OA–relevant clinical proxy (phenotyping_reported: total hip replacement) and it provides an explicit discrimination metric (AUROC 0.66 with CI) with stated basic covariates (age, sex), even though this appears to be a full-model AUROC rather than PRS-only. In contrast, PGS004478 matches the hip OA concept via ICD label (M16 coxarthrosis) but provides no AUROC/R2 at all (only an OR≈1.30) and has unknown covariates, making its performance evidence and comparability weaker on the visible fields despite the larger training/validation sizes and genome-wide LDpred2 construction.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target trait (same PheCode 428.1 CHF NOS; same EFO; same phenotyping_reported), come from the same publication and cohort context (MVP; same ancestry distribution; same covariates age/sex/20 PCs; same validation n=31,804), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model C-index, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With those near-clone conditions, the only differentiators are small performance/effect-size differences: PGS005083 has a slightly higher full-model C-index (0.75368 vs 0.75325) and slightly higher OR per SD (1.455 vs 1.443) than PGS005076. These gaps are small, so confidence is low, but they favor PGS005083.

Both candidates target the same endpoint with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Hodgkin's disease / Hodgkins lymphoma), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes (n=736 train; n=775 eval), and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), so endpoint fidelity and leakage risk do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; we must rely on the available full-model/effect-size evidence within this sibling pair. PGS000639 shows consistently stronger discrimination and effect size than PGS000637: higher AUROC (0.62 vs 0.574), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0276 vs 0.013), higher per-SD OR (1.476 vs 1.3), and higher top-1% OR (2.64 vs 1.67). Although PGS000637 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants, the domain guidance prioritizes empirical performance within same-endpoint siblings over method label/variant count when PRS-only metrics are absent. Both candidates target the exact same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all age-related macular degeneration), use the same method (PRS-CS), the same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1-10), and have identical EUR evaluation context and validation sample size (n=163,011), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only weakly comparable. Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to multiple myeloma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and are near-clones structurally (GWAS-significant variants, 23 SNPs, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL). Both candidates are near-clones: same myocardial infarction PheCode 411.2 endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned), same method (ldpred), same variant count (1,286,612), same cohorts (MVP), same covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same ancestry distributions, and same validation sample size (n=30,379). Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma) and both are sparse GWAS-hit style scores with similar variant counts (PGS002306: 23 vs PGS000653: 22) and EUR-only evaluation. Both candidates align to the target (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia), but PGS000077 has stronger endpoint fidelity via an explicit incident diagnosis phenotype (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”) and shows a stronger PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.45, CI 1.31–1.61) than PGS000645’s per-SD OR 1.358 (CI 1.113–1.657). Both candidates map cleanly to systemic lupus erythematosus (same trait_reported and trait_efo) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the visible AUROC values (0.65 for PGS000754; 0.79 for PGS000196) are full-model and not reliably comparable as PRS evidence. Overall, PGS000754 is better-supported on endpoint fidelity and model structure; confidence is moderate because both lack PRS-only performance metrics and covariates are unknown.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all multiple sclerosis). Both candidates target the same endpoint (myocardial infarction PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported matches), come from the same publication, use the same basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same training cohort (MVP), identical validation size (n=30,379) and similar ancestry distributions—so endpoint fidelity and transportability are essentially tied. Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo = melanoma) and use the same method family (genome-wide significant variants) with similar EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry. Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_reported/trait_efo, same phenotyping_reported string, same method_name PRSCS, same evaluation ancestry distribution MAE 100%, same validation_sample_size n=94,651, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 with covariates unknown), so evidence is thin and differences are small. Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to multiple sclerosis (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match). Both candidates align cleanly to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple sclerosis) and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so the reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence. Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo match; phenotyping_reported identical aside from a typo) and come from the same publication with the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). PGS001298 has directly comparable PRS-only performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.5757; PGS-only R2=0.0115) with basic covariates and a clear obesity endpoint (TTE obesity), allowing a heritability-ceiling sanity check and avoiding reliance on full-model metrics. Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target trait (myocardial infarction; PheCode 411.2) with the same phenotyping_reported, trait_efo, covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), training cohort (MVP), ancestry distribution, and validation sample size (n=30,379), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model C-index/AUC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo match; phenotyping_reported identical aside from spelling) and come from the same publication with the same ancestry distribution, cohort list, and validation sample size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is discounted). PGS001298 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence for the target trait obesity: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.57573; PGS R2 0.01146) with basic covariates and these are sanity-consistent with the provided local h2_obs ceiling (~0.006–0.0062) in the sense of being small and not obviously inflated by heavy clinical packaging. PGS005235 has tighter endpoint fidelity to the target obesity: despite the broader trait_reported label (“Adiposity”), its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Obesity (phecode: 278.1)” with trait_efo=obesity, whereas PGS002033 uses a broader administrative/nutrition bundle phenotype (“Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation”) mapped to multiple EFOs (obesity/overweight/overnutrition), which is less specific to obesity. PGS001298 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.5757) and PGS-only R² (0.01146) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), and these PRS-only metrics are sanity-consistent with the obesity h2_obs ceiling (~0.005–0.006) in the provided domain note (at least not wildly inflated). PGS001298’s main drawback is being a pan-trait UKB framework sparse score and time-to-event phenotype, but given PGS004447’s missing comparable metrics and unclear covariate context, PGS001298 has the stronger documented support overall.

PGS004447 has tighter endpoint fidelity to the target obesity: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are ICD10 E66 (Obesity), whereas PGS002033 uses a broader administrative bundle (“Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation”) and maps to multiple EFO traits (obesity/overweight/overnutrition), which is less specific. Overall, the decision hinges on phenotype specificity, giving PGS004447 a narrow edge despite missing covariate details.

Both candidates have good endpoint fidelity for the target trait (phenotyping_reported and trait_reported are Osteoporosis; EUR-only evaluation). Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to obesity (PGS005235 uses an obesity phecode 278.1; PGS004447 uses ICD10 E66) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size and study/metadata cleanliness drive the decision. PGS001255 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PGS-only R² (0.01341), enabling a clean comparison and a heritability-ceiling sanity check (well below the provided h2_obs=0.0048, noting scale differences but no obvious inflation). Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Osteoporosis”) and are EUR-only in development and evaluation, with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either. PGS000549 is the better-supported match to the target trait (ovarian neoplasm) on endpoint fidelity: its trait_efo is exactly "ovarian neoplasm" and phenotyping_reported is a direct diagnosis label ("Malignant neoplasm of ovary"). PGS000082 is the better-supported choice for the broad target “ovarian neoplasm” because its phenotyping is a direct disease endpoint (“Incident ovarian cancer”), whereas PGS003394 is packaged as horizon-specific prediction (“10-year ovarian cancer risks”), which domain guidance flags as a negative (risk-wrapper/absolute-risk packaging rather than clean disease status). PGS000549 is the better-supported choice for the target trait “ovarian neoplasm” because its concept alignment is tighter: trait_efo matches exactly (ovarian neoplasm) and the reported/phenotyped endpoint is a direct malignant ovary neoplasm diagnosis. Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported ovarian cancer; trait_efo ovarian carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident ovarian cancer) and share the same EUR-only evaluation context and essentially identical covariates, so endpoint fidelity and transportability do not differentiate them. Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident pancreatic cancer), have identical ancestry evaluation (EUR 100%), identical variant count (22), and essentially identical reported discrimination/effect size (full-model AUROC 0.745; C-index ~0.742–0.743; HR per SD 1.49) with the same covariate set including family history and smoking/BMI (so full-model AUROC is not PRS-only for either). Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and both use 22 variants with similar GWAS ancestry makeup. PGS000663 is from a pancreatic-cancer-focused risk prediction study and shows broader evaluation ancestry (EAS+EUR) with a comparable per-SD effect size (OR 1.44) and less overt family-history packaging, so it is better-supported as a standalone pancreatic cancer PRS despite the smaller validation sample.

Both candidates target the same disease concept (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and use the same sparse GWAS-hits construction (22 variants; genome-wide significant variants) with the same listed development cohorts, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator). PGS000083 has a more endpoint-faithful, generic incident cancer phenotype ("Incident pancreatic cancer") versus PGS000663’s horizon-conditioned packaging ("Pancreatic cancer (0–10 years of follow-up)"), which domain guidance flags as a weaker, deployment-style endpoint. PGS000083 also shows slightly stronger PRS signal via effect size (HR 1.49 vs OR 1.44) and is evaluated in a much larger validation sample (391,491 vs 956), while PGS000663 additionally mixes in more clinical/mediator-like covariates (e.g., diabetic status, fasting status) alongside the horizon framing. Overall, PGS000083 is better supported on endpoint fidelity and robustness, with only moderate confidence because both lack PRS-only performance metrics and the AUROC values are full-model and not directly comparable.

Both candidates align to Parkinson disease by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000903 has a cleaner generic PD endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Parkinson's disease") versus PGS003763 being explicitly incident PD (time-to-event framing), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic PD target. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC cannot be used as a PRS-comparable metric; however PGS000903 provides substantially richer supporting evidence (multi-cohort disease GWAS meta-analysis context with listed training/development cohorts, many more variants: 1805 vs 44, and a strong stratification OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25) whereas PGS003763 has no training information (samples_training N/A, no cohorts) and only a single HR tertile contrast (1.72). Covariates are basic in both (PCs/array; PGS000903 also includes age/sex), so covariate leakage is not a differentiator. Overall, PGS000903 is better supported on endpoint generality and evidence richness.

Both candidates are from the same Lancet Neurol PD GWAS meta-analysis, with identical trait/phenotyping alignment (Parkinson’s disease), identical basic covariates (PCs 1–5, age, sex), identical training cohorts and training N, and the same validation sample size (n=999), so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values are not clean PRS-comparable; however, PGS000903 has stronger supporting evidence via substantially larger variant count (1805 C+T vs 90 genome-wide significant hits) and includes additional effect-size/stratification metrics (R²=0.054 and OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25) that PGS000902 lacks, while also showing a higher reported AUROC (0.692 vs 0.651) under the same covariate set. Given the absence of PRS-only metrics, the decision leans on structural signal and richer performance/effect-size reporting, favoring PGS000903.

PGS005217 is better supported for the target concept despite a slight label mismatch (peripheral artery disease vs peripheral vascular disease): its phenotyping is a clear clinical endpoint (incident PAD) and it comes from a disease-focused PAD/MALE study with broad multi-cohort development and multi-ancestry evaluation. It also provides a strong PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.66) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), whereas PGS002055 is a UKB portability-framework score for an unspecified PVD phenotype with only a very small PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0175) and no effect-size/AUC evidence. Neither reports PGS-only AUC/R2, so the stronger endpoint-focused evidence package and effect size favor PGS005217 over the weaker, unspecified framework phenotype in PGS002055.

PGS003394 is the better-supported match to the target ovarian neoplasm because its endpoint is explicitly epithelial ovarian cancer (a core/major ovarian carcinoma subtype) and it comes from an ovarian-cancer–focused modeling study with stated training size (n=31,252) and broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR), supporting transportability. PGS000793 is derived by inverting weights from another score (PGS000082) and is embedded in a pan-cancer risk-factor integration framework with explicit family history and multiple non-genetic covariates, making its reported discrimination (C-index/AUROC ~0.66) less interpretable as PRS evidence; it also lacks a training sample size. Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R², and the full-model C-index values are close/incomparable given different covariate packaging, so confidence is low but the cleaner disease-focused construction and multi-ancestry evaluation favor PGS003394.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified”), identical study context (same UKB portability paper), identical training size (n=391,124), covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), and identical ancestry distribution and validation size, so the decision rests on PRS-comparable performance and structural signals. PGS002055 shows higher PRS-comparable partial correlation (partial-r 0.0175 vs 0.0151 for PGS001843) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (599,514 vs 242), which is generally favorable for polygenic disease prediction when other fields are matched. With no PGS-only AUC/R2 available for either, these modest but consistent advantages make PGS002055 better supported.

PGS003587 is better supported for the target trait preeclampsia because its endpoint evidence is more coherent: although its trait_reported is gestational hypertension, its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia” and trait_efo maps to preeclampsia, aligning with the target. In contrast, PGS004593 has an exact trait_reported (“Preeclampsia”) but its phenotyping_reported is “Gestational hypertension,” creating a more direct endpoint mismatch on the primary fidelity field. Both candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect sizes and study context matter: PGS003587 shows a slightly stronger per-SD association (OR 1.20 vs HR 1.16) and provides clearer development context (multi-cohort training list and a stated training N), whereas PGS004593 has N/A training size and no listed training/development cohorts. PGS004593’s larger validation sample is only a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the phenotype-fidelity advantage of PGS003587.

PGS004155 is better supported for the generic target trait “prostate cancer” because its phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint (“Prostate cancer”) with no added covariates (covariates=0), making the reported evidence less likely to be inflated by risk-wrapper packaging. It also provides PRS-relevant effect-size evidence (OR per SD ≈2.17) and uses an ensemble-style method (MultiPRS), a positive structural signal. In contrast, PGS005237’s phenotyping_reported is explicitly horizon-conditioned (“5-year incident prostate cancer”) and its covariates indicate age-specific absolute-risk adjustment (“Age-specific absolute risk adjusted by PGS relative risk”), which is a strong comparability/leakage warning; its higher full-model AUROC (0.781 vs 0.705) is therefore not reliable as PRS-only evidence, especially since neither candidate reports PGS-only AUROC/R².

PGS004155 is better supported for the generic target trait “prostate cancer” because its phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint (“Prostate cancer”) with no added covariates (covariates=0), making the reported evidence less likely to be inflated by clinical risk packaging. In contrast, PGS005238 uses a horizon-conditioned endpoint (“5-year incident prostate cancer”) and explicitly wraps the score in age-specific absolute-risk adjustment (“Age-specific absolute risk adjusted by PGS relative risk”), which is a strong comparability/leakage warning signal; its higher full-model AUROC (0.789 vs 0.705) is therefore not clean PRS evidence, especially since neither candidate reports PGS-only AUROC/R2. Both are trained in UKB with similar training N (~10k) and similar validation size, so endpoint fidelity and covariate cleanliness drive the decision in favor of PGS004155.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (both: prostate carcinoma; 5-year incident prostate cancer), study context (same publication), training cohort/size (UKB; n=10,000), ancestry distribution, validation size (n=184,010), and both lack PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC, which is discounted especially given the age-specific absolute-risk packaging covariate statement in both). With those major fields tied, PGS005238 has the only consistent edge: slightly higher reported AUROC in the selected European validation record (0.789 vs 0.781) and a more genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with higher variant count (964,607 vs 517,551), which is a favorable structural signal when other evidence is indistinguishable.

Both candidates come from the same Nat Med study, use the same method (PRS-CS), have essentially identical evaluation context (EUR-only evaluation, same validation N=25,582), identical phenotyping_reported (Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia), and similarly clean/basic covariates (maternal age, age^2, PCs), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either—so performance must be judged mainly by endpoint alignment and effect size. For the target trait preeclampsia, PGS003586 has the most faithful trait_reported label (Pre-eclampsia) and also shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20 for PGS003587). PGS003587 is labeled gestational hypertension (despite the same phenotyping string), making it slightly less directly aligned to the target and with weaker effect-size evidence.

PGS005217 is better supported for the target concept despite a slight label mismatch (peripheral artery disease vs peripheral vascular disease): its phenotyping is a clear clinical endpoint (incident PAD) and it comes from a disease-focused PAD study with broad multi-cohort development and multi-ancestry evaluation. It also reports a strong PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.66), which is meaningful PRS-discrimination evidence even though only a full-model C-index is shown (and PGS-only AUC/R2 are missing). In contrast, PGS001843 is an exact-label match (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified) but is from a UKB portability/framework paper with a very sparse 242-variant score and only a very weak PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0151), providing limited evidence of useful PRS signal. Both lack PGS-only AUC/R2, so the stronger endpoint-focused evidence package and effect size favor PGS005217.

Both candidates align to the target trait (Parkinson disease) at trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000902 has cleaner generic disease endpoint wording (phenotyping_reported: "Parkinson's disease") versus PGS003763 being explicitly "Incident Parkinson Disease" in a frailty-focused time-to-event context. Neither reports PRS-comparable PGS-only AUC/R2, so performance can’t be compared on the preferred metrics; PGS000902’s only AUROC (0.651) is full-model and thus not a valid PRS-only differentiator, while PGS003763 reports only an HR (1.72 high vs low tertile) which is harder to compare across designs. With metrics near-tied in comparability, structural/study-support signals favor PGS000902: it is derived from a large, disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis with explicit training/development cohorts listed and a larger GWAS-hit set (90 variants vs 44), whereas PGS003763 has no training sample/cohort information (samples_training N/A; cohorts empty) and looks more like an application study where the PRS is one component in an exposure/interaction analysis.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all psoriasis) and both are UKB-based framework/portability-style scores with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). The key differentiator is comparable PRS performance evidence: PGS001312 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6916; PGS-only R2=0.0523) whereas PGS002083 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0632) and no PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, which the policy treats as missing evidence that cannot be substituted by other model metrics. Although PGS002083 uses many more variants and a genome-wide shrinkage method, the lack of PRS-comparable discrimination metrics makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001312.

PGS003586 has clearly better endpoint fidelity to the target trait preeclampsia: its phenotyping_reported is “Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia” and trait_reported matches, whereas PGS004593’s phenotyping_reported is “Gestational hypertension,” which is a related but non-identical hypertensive disorder of pregnancy and thus a phenotype mismatch for preeclampsia. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size and study support matter more: PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD association (OR 1.31) than PGS004593 (HR 1.16), suggesting more discriminative PRS signal. PGS003586 also provides a clearer disease-focused multi-cohort development context (multiple listed training/development cohorts and a stated training n=212,034), while PGS004593 has no training sample size and no cohorts listed. Although PGS004593 has a much larger validation sample, validation size is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the phenotype mismatch and weaker effect size.

PGS001312 is the better-supported choice for generic psoriasis because its endpoint is a direct disease phenotype (phenotyping_reported: "Psoriasis") whereas PGS001313 is explicitly time-to-event ("TTE psoriasis" / "Psoriasis (time-to-event)"), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease target. Both are otherwise near-clones (same pan-trait UKB framework publication, same training n=269,704, same covariates, same ancestry distribution, same validation n=67,425), so performance becomes the tie-break: PGS001312 reports higher PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6916 vs 0.6729; PGS-only R2 0.0523 vs 0.0497; incremental AUROC 0.1451 vs 0.1385). Although PGS001313 has more variants (578 vs 204), that structural advantage does not outweigh the combination of better endpoint fidelity and consistently stronger PRS-only performance in PGS001312.

PGS001280 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.60765) and PGS-only R2 (0.01403) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), allowing clean interpretation and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS003861 has an exact disease label and is disease-focused in a Han Chinese cohort, but it lacks PRS-only metrics entirely (only a full-model AUROC=0.765, covariates unknown), so its discrimination is not comparable and could be covariate-driven; the reported OR is quantile-based and not an OR-per-SD substitute. Despite PGS001280’s framework-paper penalty and time-to-event phenotype, the presence of standalone PRS metrics and multi-ancestry evaluation support makes it the stronger evidenced choice here.

PGS001313 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.6729 with CI) and PGS-only R² (0.04966), whereas PGS002083 provides no AUROC/R² at all and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0632), which is less directly comparable to standard PRS discrimination metrics. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (psoriasis; PGS001313 is time-to-event but still psoriasis), and covariates are similarly basic (age/sex/PCs/array vs age/sex/PCs plus deprivation/birth date). Although both come from UKB framework/portability-style papers, the presence of clean PGS-only metrics in PGS001313 outweighs PGS002083’s larger variant count and training N given the missing PRS-comparable metrics in PGS002083.

PGS001280 is the better-supported match to the target trait pulmonary embolism because its endpoint is more specific and aligned (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: "PE (time-to-event)" / "TTE PE" with trait_efo exactly pulmonary embolism), whereas PGS001279 is endpoint-broader/less cleanly aligned (trait_efo includes both pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis and trait_reported is framed as "previously: Blood clot in the lung"). On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001280 also has slightly stronger PGS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.60765; PGS-only R2 0.01403) than PGS001279 (0.60034; 0.01146), with both using similarly basic covariates and the same pan-trait UKB framework context. The larger validation N for PGS001279 is a weak tie-break and doesn’t outweigh the cleaner PE-specific phenotype and modestly better PRS-only metrics of PGS001280.

Both candidates align to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (same trait_reported/trait_efo), but PGS001791 provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.005929) that is sanity-consistent with the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.0039) and at least quantifies standalone PRS signal, whereas PGS004695 reports no AUC/R2 at all (only an HR high-vs-low quintile=3.78, which is less directly comparable across studies). Structurally, PGS001791 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with ~910k variants and is developed across many biobanks, while PGS004695 is a sparse 23-SNP genome-wide-significant score from an exposure-focused cohort study with more non-genetic covariate packaging (education, smoking, pack-years, BMI). Given cleaner PRS-specific metric reporting and stronger polygenic construction, PGS001791 is better supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates map to the same target concept (trait_efo=retinal detachment), but PGS001137 has cleaner, PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R2=0.00663 (and these are plausibly below the local h2_obs ceiling ~0.0042 as a sanity check, at least not wildly inflated), whereas PGS002040 provides no AUROC/R2 and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0276), which is less directly comparable to standard PRS discrimination metrics. Endpoint fidelity is similar, though PGS002040’s reported phenotype is broader (“Retinal detachments and defects”) than PGS001137’s direct “Retinal detachment.” While PGS002040 has a stronger structural setup (LDpred2 with genome-wide variants and larger training N), the lack of PRS-comparable metrics makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001137.

PGS003861 is a direct, disease-focused pulmonary embolism score with exact trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported alignment to the target and a strong reported risk gradient (OR 5.08 for a quantile contrast), whereas PGS001279 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank “813 traits” sparse framework (snpnet) and has only modest PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.600, PGS R2 0.011) plus a trait_efo that explicitly mixes pulmonary embolism with deep vein thrombosis (less endpoint-specific). However, confidence is low because PGS003861 lacks PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R2; only a full-model AUROC 0.765 with unknown covariates), making its discrimination evidence less cleanly comparable than PGS001279’s explicit PGS-only metrics.

PGS000923 is better supported for the target trait sarcoidosis because its concept mapping is coherent across fields (trait_efo=sarcoidosis; phenotyping_reported=TTE sarcoidosis) and it reports clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64561 and PGS-only R2=0.018), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS001872 has a notable endpoint mismatch (trait_efo=skin sarcoidosis) and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 entirely (only partial-r=0.0199), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable despite having more variants and larger training N.

PGS001030 is better supported for the broad target trait “pulmonary fibrosis” because it matches the umbrella endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all pulmonary fibrosis) and provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6252; PGS-only R2=0.0142), which are interpretable and below the heritability ceiling sanity check. It also has explicit training information (UKB, n=269,704) and multi-ancestry evaluation records (though selected EUR). In contrast, PGS004695 targets the narrower subtype idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (incident-only) and reports no PRS-comparable AUC/R2—only a quintile HR—making cross-model PRS performance comparison weaker despite its large evaluation N; its publication context is also exposure-focused, suggesting the PRS may be auxiliary rather than a primary disease-PRS optimization.

Both candidates are essentially matched on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), training cohort and size (UKB; n=391,124), and evaluation ancestry mix/validation N (n=19,445), so performance and structural signals drive the choice. PGS002040 shows higher PRS-comparable performance via partial correlation (partial-r 0.0276 vs 0.0218 for PGS001833) with similar CIs, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far broader variant coverage (706,872 vs 3,737), which is generally favorable when other fields are identical. With no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported for either, these two signals make PGS002040 better supported overall.

PGS001791 is better supported for the target because its endpoint is the clinically specific subtype (Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) with coherent trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported alignment, and it comes from a broad multi-biobank development context (many cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage approach with very large variant coverage (910,439), which is structurally favorable versus the sparse UKB framework score. Although PGS001030 reports stronger explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6252; PGS R2 0.0142) than PGS001791’s covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.005929), PGS001030 is from the known pan-trait ‘813 traits’ UKB sparse snpnet framework with only 51 variants—an archetype that is penalized for weaker disease-focused support and generalization despite having multi-ancestry evaluation. Both use only basic covariates, and both are under the heritability ceiling, so the decision hinges on endpoint specificity and study/method structure favoring PGS001791 over the framework sparse alternative.

Both candidates are near-clones: same schizophrenia endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same GWAS ancestry mix and EUR-only evaluation, and similarly basic covariates; neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC=0.6, which is not PRS-comparable). With endpoints and covariates effectively tied, the differentiators are effect size and structural signals: PGS000133 shows a stronger per-SD OR (1.691 vs 1.483 for PGS000134), indicating stronger PRS discrimination, while the slightly larger variant count and validation N for PGS000134 are weaker tie-breakers here.

PGS001137 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R2=0.00663 (no covariates), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling and interpreted cleanly. PGS001833 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 entirely and only provides a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0218), making its predictive performance less directly comparable for PRS selection. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (both map to EFO retinal detachment; PGS001833 is slightly broader as 'retinal detachments and defects'), and covariates are basic in both, so the decisive difference is the presence of clear PRS-only metrics in PGS001137 versus missing PRS-comparable discrimination metrics in PGS001833.

Both candidates target rheumatoid arthritis with identical trait_reported/trait_efo and the same phenotyping_reported (Seropositive RA), ancestry distribution, training cohort (UKB), training size (n=820), covariates=0, and validation size (n=90,274), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model metrics, which are not ideal for PRS comparison). Given this near-clone setup, PGS004163 is better supported because it shows consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence in the selected European validation record (higher AUROC 0.7469 vs 0.7283; higher R² 0.1376 vs 0.1220; higher OR per SD 2.46 vs 2.37) and it uses an ensemble/multi-score approach (MultiPRS) with a larger variant set (778,275 vs 373,627), which is a positive structural signal when endpoints and covariates are the same.

Both candidates are near-clones: same schizophrenia endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS EAS 6%/EUR 94%; evaluation EUR 100%), same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With endpoint and covariates effectively identical, PGS000136 has modestly stronger reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.64 vs 0.60) and a substantially higher variant count (833,502 vs 604,645), which is a meaningful within-method structural advantage. PGS000133’s larger validation n (33,694 vs 18,461) is only a weak tie-break and doesn’t outweigh the higher AUROC/variant coverage for PGS000136.

PGS000922 is the better-supported sarcoidosis PRS because it has clear PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.64282 and PGS-only R2=0.01741) with basic covariates, allowing a direct assessment of PRS signal and a heritability-ceiling sanity check (R2 well below h2_liability≈0.107). In contrast, PGS001872 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 entirely and reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0199), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination; additionally its trait_efo is explicitly mismatched to the target ("skin sarcoidosis" vs sarcoidosis) while PGS000922 maps cleanly to sarcoidosis. Both are UKB framework-style scores with similar ancestry evaluation patterns, so the decision is driven by endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-only metrics favoring PGS000922.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), identical covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), same training cohort (MGI) and same training/validation sizes. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; we must rely on within-family empirical signals. PGS000471 shows consistently stronger validation evidence than PGS000470: higher AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557), higher pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154), better top-1% vs rest OR (3.77 vs 2.45), and higher per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308). It also uses lassosum with slightly more variants (7 vs 5), a mild structural advantage. Given the near-clone design and small AUROC gap, confidence is moderate but favors PGS000471.

PGS002745 has the cleaner endpoint match to the target trait: phenotyping_reported is simply “Rheumatoid arthritis,” aligning directly with the generic rheumatoid arthritis target, whereas PGS004049’s phenotyping_reported is “Seropositive RA,” a subtype restriction. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (both only show full-model AUROC/R2), so the higher full-model AUROC/R² in PGS004049 is not a reliable PRS-comparable advantage, especially given the covariate ambiguity (PGS004049 lists covariates as “0” while PGS002745 uses basic sex+PCs). PGS002745 also shows broader multi-ancestry evaluation (EAS/EUR/MAE/MAO) versus PGS004049’s EUR/SAS evaluation, supporting transportability. Confidence is low because both lack PRS-only metrics and PGS004049 has stronger reported full-model performance and effect sizes, but those are not directly comparable PRS evidence.

PGS004163 is better supported for the target trait despite both lacking PRS-only AUC/R2: it has stronger endpoint fidelity to a clinically specific RA definition (phenotyping_reported: seropositive RA, aligning with RA and a listed heritability-matched ICD10 M05 subtype) and provides supportive PRS signal via effect sizes (OR per SD ~2.46, β reported), whereas PGS002745 reports no effect sizes. The reported AUROC/R2 for both are full-model (not PRS-comparable), but PGS004163’s full-model AUROC is higher (0.747 vs 0.66) and it uses no covariates (covariates=0), avoiding covariate-driven inflation concerns relative to PGS002745’s sex+PC adjustment. PGS004163 also has a structurally stronger, genome-wide ensemble-style construction (MultiPRS; 778k variants) versus PGS002745’s sparse P+T (2,575 variants). PGS002745’s advantage is broader evaluation ancestry mix, but its small validation size (n=3,887) and weaker/less informative performance package make it less supported overall.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry (EUR-only), same training cohort (MGI), same training N (6,005), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and same validation size (5,500), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given that, the best available discriminative evidence favors PGS000470: higher full-model AUROC (0.557 vs 0.524), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0154 vs 0.00141), stronger per-SD OR (1.308 vs 1.09), and stronger top-1% vs rest OR (2.45 vs 1.48). Although PGS000469 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants, its observed effect-size and full-model metrics are consistently weaker in the same evaluation setting, so PGS000470 is better-supported on the visible record fields.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target/endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS EAS+EUR; EUR evaluation), and same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Given this, the main differentiators are the reported effect size and full-model AUROC: PGS000136 shows higher AUROC (0.64 vs 0.60) and a stronger OR per SD (1.7 vs 1.483), which is meaningful supportive evidence of stronger PRS signal, whereas PGS000134’s larger validation n (44,436 vs 18,461) is only a weak tie-break per the provided policy. Therefore PGS000136 is better supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet framework paper, with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (269,704), covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation N (67,425), and both report clean PRS-only metrics. PGS000923 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 (0.6456/0.018 vs 0.6428/0.0174) and more variants (22 vs 12), but it is explicitly a time-to-event endpoint (phenotyping_reported: TTE sarcoidosis; trait_reported: time-to-event), which is a weaker match for the generic target trait ‘sarcoidosis’ than PGS000922’s direct disease endpoint labeling (phenotyping_reported: Sarcoidosis). Given the small performance differences and the domain guidance prioritizing endpoint fidelity over marginal metric gains, PGS000922 is better supported for the target trait.

In contrast, PGS000760 has a clear phenotype mismatch in phenotyping_reported (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), i.e., a treatment-induced, non-vitiligo endpoint; its reported metric is a meta-analysis p-value and an HR=1.41 that pertains to that therapy-specific hypothyroidism outcome, making it less comparable for vitiligo risk prediction despite larger training N and basic PC covariates.
